problems.stem: In Keller's ARCS model, which component is primarily about capturing curiosity at the start of instruction?
problems.explanation: Attention is the entry point of the ARCS model and focuses on arousing curiosity or interest.

problems.stem: Which design choice most directly improves relevance?
options: Opening with a surprising but unrelated joke
Showing how the lesson connects to the learner's real job tasks and goals
Increasing the number of badges awarded
Reducing every task to drill-only repetition
problems.explanation: Relevance grows when learners can see why the material matters in their own context.

problems.stem: What design move most directly supports confidence in ARCS?
options: Providing clear expectations and progressive success experiences
Removing all feedback so learners rely on instinct
problems.explanation: Confidence grows when learners understand the target and experience achievable success along the way.

problems.stem: Why can excessive external rewards sometimes weaken intrinsic motivation?
options: Because rewards are never useful in any learning context
Because the activity can become framed as something done only for the reward
Because learners stop caring about feedback altogether
Because extrinsic motivation always produces deep transfer
problems.explanation: The overjustification effect occurs when an activity once valued for its own sake is reinterpreted as something done merely for reward.
